name: Yi Guo
title: Professor and Thomas E. Hattrick Chair Professor
fitReason: Combines model-based control with learned prediction and motion planning for actual cooperating robots. The dynamic ball-passing work offers a concrete robot-learning/control connection, alongside multi-robot coordination.

physicalEvidence.summary: The official IROS 2025 program describes real-world ball passing between two autonomously controlled mobile manipulators, combining analytical models and neural learning for throwing/catching. First-author code specifies LSTM landing prediction, MLP throwing parameters, OptiTrack and RoboMaster hardware. The lab currently lists first author Xinchi Huang and coauthor Yifan Mao as students. Detailed numerical performance and a complete paper were not accessed.

shortVisit.summary: No current invitation for external visiting students or short research internships was found in the checked faculty, research and news pages. The lab news records summer visitors in 2018; that is historical precedent only, with no current opportunity credit.

scoreReasons.fit: Direct neural learning for cooperative mobile manipulation and decentralized control; less emphasis on general-purpose foundation policies.
scoreReasons.physical: Official real-experiment abstract and released hardware-oriented code, tied to current students in the same lab. No numerical performance claim or 2026 ViT hardware inference.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: Only historical summer visitors, without a verified current inquiry invitation or external-master's route.
scoreReasons.freshness: Current faculty/student pages and official 2026 technical listing; most clearly verified learning-hardware work is IROS 2025. The 2026 listing inconsistency is retained.
